name: Josh Riley
page_title: Josh Riley's Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Democratic, Working Families for U.S. House (NY) - District 19

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "Protect women’s right to make their own healthcare decisions"

"Following the Supreme Court’s decision in Dobbs, which overturned Roe v. Wade, Josh set forth a detailed plan for legislative and regulatory action to protect women’s access to abortion care, and he has been a leading advocate for protecting access to abortion medications, including by urging the Justice Department and the Food & Drug Administration to act."

"Josh has received support from leading advocacy organizations, including Planned Parenthood, NARAL Pro-Choice America, the National Organization of Women, Vote ProChoice, and the Family Planning Action Fund."

positions.question: Do you support expanding federal funding to support social safety net programs such as Social Security and Medicare?

evidence.text: "Josh has received support from Social Security Works and the National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare."
"Seniors have earned the right to retire with dignity. Josh will never cut a penny from Social Security or Medicare. He believes that retirement programs should be strengthened, not weakened"
"Strengthen Medicare to cover hearing, dental, and vision services"
"Strengthen the care economy so seniors can access the long-term care they need and their families deserve."

positions.question: Do you support a decrease in income taxes in order to balance the budget?

evidence.text: "Cut taxes for the Middle Class so working families keep more of their own money"
"Require the wealthy and big corporations to pay their fair share so we can reduce the deficit and invest in necessary public services"

"The Middle Class needs a tax cut; billionaires and big corporations don’t. Josh believes it is unacceptable that hedge fund managers pay lower tax rates than janitors, and he believes the tax code should be reformed to be simpler, fairer, and less of a burden for working families."

positions.question: Do you support a wealth tax in order to pay for public programs?

evidence.text: "Create a wealth surtax on incomes over $5 million and trusts/estates valued at more than $25 million"
"Require the wealthy and big corporations to pay their fair share so we can reduce the deficit and invest in necessary public services"
"Require the wealthy to pay their fair share into these programs"

"The Middle Class needs a tax cut; billionaires and big corporations don’t. Josh believes it is unacceptable that hedge fund managers pay lower tax rates than janitors, and he believes the tax code should be reformed to be simpler, fairer, and less of a burden for working families."

positions.question: Do you support the regulation of indirect campaign contributions from corporations, unions, and individuals?

evidence.text: "As counsel in the U.S. Senate, Josh worked on a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United, the disastrous Supreme Court case that opened the floodgates to dark money in our politics. As an attorney in private practice, Josh filed a brief in the U.S. Supreme Court to strengthen campaign finance laws"
"Josh has received support from End Citizens United, which recognized Josh’s commitment to refusing corporate PACs and reforming our campaign finance system."

"Our campaign finance system is a cesspool. Let’s drain it. Josh believes the corrupting influence of corporate money and dark money is the root of all evil in our politics. Special interests buy seats for politicians who then vote for the special interests’ bottom lines, not yours."
"Stop Big Money’s corrupting influence in our politics"

positions.question: Do you support protecting government officials, including law enforcement officers, from personal liability in civil lawsuits concerning alleged misconduct?

evidence.text: "As counsel in the U.S. Senate, Josh worked to bring Democrats and Republicans together to advance legislation that was supported by the National Sheriffs Association and National Association of Police Organizations"

"Josh comes from a law enforcement family, so he knows first-hand the sacrifices our law enforcement and first responders make to keep our communities safe. Josh is adamantly opposed to proposals to "defund the police," and he believes that public safety requires more resources, not fewer."

positions.question: Do you support increasing defense spending?

evidence.text: "Use defense funds wisely and efficiently"

positions.question: Do you support federal spending as a means of promoting economic growth (e.g. grants, tax incentives)?

evidence.text: "Create good jobs building the American-made products we need to fight climate change."
"Invest in American manufacturing, making the things the world needs right here at home"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

evidence.text: "Congress should invest in the construction of new affordable housing. Our building trades unions can do the work."

"Every single child deserves safe shelter. We must (a) expand access to affordable housing (by building more of it with union labor sustainably) and (b) implement the infrastructure law to get lead out of homes and water."

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "Big corporations are raking in major profits by jacking prices and blaming inflation. We must do more to prevent this rampant practice and give working families the break they deserve."
"Crack down on price gouging so corporations can’t profit on artificially increased prices"

"Merck forecasts profits of over $57B this year. Now they’re suing to roll back the Inflation Reduction Act so they can price gouge seniors to make even more. It’s corporate greed, and I’m fighting against it."
"The Inflation Reduction Act will create good jobs in renewable energy right here in Upstate New York. I support it. Marc Molinaro does not."

positions.question: Do you support requiring a government-issued identification in order to vote at the polls?

evidence.text: "I'm honored to have the Voter Protection Project's endorsement in this campaign. There's no right more fundamental to a functioning Democracy than the right to vote and have your voice heard. That's why I worked to strengthen the Voting Rights Act when I was counsel in the U.S. Senate, and it's why I'll always fight to strengthen our Democracy when I'm in Congress."
"Josh has received support from leading pro-Democracy groups, including End Citizens United/Let America Vote, Defend the Vote, and the Voter Protection Project."
"Protect access to the ballot, particularly for service-members and communities whose rights to vote historically have been suppressed"

positions.question: Do you support government funding for the development of renewable energy (e.g. solar, wind, geo-thermal)?

evidence.text: "Create good jobs building the American-made products we need to fight climate change."
"Establish energy independence, including by ending our reliance on fossil fuels."
"The Inflation Reduction Act will create good jobs in renewable energy right here in Upstate New York. I support it. Marc Molinaro does not."

positions.question: Do you support the federal government allowing permits for drilling on public lands?

evidence.text: "Establish energy independence, including by ending our reliance on fossil fuels."

"From superstorms to wildfire smoke to deadly flooding, Upstate New Yorkers have experienced the climate crisis firsthand. But Marc Molinaro cashes checks from Big Oil and voted to kill the clean energy projects here in Upstate New York. It makes no sense."
"Slashing investments in clean-energy manufacturing is great for Big Oil, but it’s terrible for the planet and for Upstate NY."

positions.question: Do you generally support gun-control legislation (e.g. red flag laws, boyfriend loopholes)?

evidence.text: "Keeping weapons of war out of schools and off the streets through appropriately tailored and constitutionally permissible legislation"
"Josh supports: Stronger background checks to keep weapons out of the hands of folks who are a danger to themselves or others"

"We can keep vulnerable populations safe from gun violence while honoring law-abiding gun owners’ Second Amendment rights. Josh served as counsel on the U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee following the massacre at Sandy Hook Elementary School, and he worked on common-sense legislation to keep communities safe."

positions.question: Do you support a government-run (e.g. single-payer) healthcare program, such as Medicare-for-All?

evidence.text: "Create a public option so that anyone who wants it can use it"

"Healthcare should be a civil right in America, not something that bankrupts so many American families. Josh believes that our healthcare system should put patients over profits. He has litigated in federal courts to improve children’s access to healthcare services, and he worked as counsel in the U.S. Senate to advance legislation to improve access to addiction treatment and mental health care."

positions.question: Do you support expanding paid family AND/OR medical leave benefits (e.g. maternity leave)?

evidence.text: "If the wealthy finally pay their fair share, we can invest in things like paid family leave and universal Pre-K. These will be some of my top priorities in Congress."
"Paid family leave shouldn’t be a luxury only available to the wealthy. No one should have to choose between taking care of a sick family member or a new baby and their job. RT if you agree."
"The best thing I ever did for my career was take paternity leave to spend time with my son. Every parent should be afforded the same opportunity. In Congress, I will fight for paid family leave."
"This is the best moment of my day. Every parent and every child should have the time and resources they need to bond. That’s why I support universal paid family leave and the child tax credit."

positions.question: Should the government be able to regulate the cost of prescription drugs?

evidence.text: "Cap the cost of critical drugs and allow Medicare greater authority to negotiate drug prices."
"Lower the cost of prescription drugs, including by ending pay-for-delay deals that jack up prices by reducing competition"

positions.question: Do you support increasing security along the southern US border?

evidence.text: "Our immigration system is completely broken, and it needs to be fixed in a way that upholds both the law and our values.
